learningObjectives.title: Revelation and the nature of God

questions.q: What is meant by the term 'revelation' in Christianity?
options: The way God makes himself known to human beings
The study of ancient religious languages
The belief that God cannot exist
The rejection of all supernatural belief
questions.explain: Revelation refers to God disclosing or making himself known to humanity.

questions.q: Christians traditionally divide revelation into which two main types?
questions.explain: Revelation is usually classified as general (through the world) or special (through direct experience).

questions.q: General revelation is the belief that God can be known through...
options: the natural world, reason and conscience
the creeds of the Church only
questions.explain: General revelation is available to everyone through creation, human reason and conscience.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of special revelation?
options: A direct vision or experience of God
Using reason to conclude God exists
Feeling awe at the size of the universe
questions.explain: Special revelation is God revealing himself directly, for example through visions, scripture or Jesus.

questions.q: The Christian belief that God is three persons in one God is called the...
questions.explain: The Trinity is the belief in one God existing as three persons.

questions.q: The three persons of the Trinity are the...
questions.explain: Christians believe in one God as Father, Son and Holy Spirit.

questions.q: To describe God as 'omnipotent' means that God is...
questions.explain: Omnipotent means God has unlimited power.

questions.q: To describe God as 'transcendent' means that God is...
options: beyond and outside the created universe
present and active within the world
questions.explain: A transcendent God exists beyond and independent of the physical universe.

questions.q: To describe God as 'immanent' means that God is...
options: present and active within the world
questions.explain: An immanent God is present in and involved with the created world.

questions.q: The Bible is divided into two main sections called the...
questions.explain: The Christian Bible is made up of the Old Testament and the New Testament.

questions.q: Christians call the Bible 'the Word of God' mainly because they believe it...
options: reveals God's message and will to humanity
was written personally by God with no human help
questions.explain: As the Word of God, the Bible is believed to communicate God's message and will.

questions.q: To say the Bible is 'inspired' by God means that...
options: God guided the human writers of its books
questions.explain: Inspiration is the belief that God influenced and guided the human authors of scripture.

questions.q: A biblical literalist is a Christian who believes that...
options: every word of the Bible is literally true
the Bible is only a collection of myths
questions.explain: Literalists accept the Bible as the exact, literal truth of God's word.

questions.q: Why do many Christians treat the Bible as a source of authority?
options: It is believed to be revealed by God and guides belief and behaviour
It is the oldest book ever written
It was written by kings and rulers
It has no connection with God
questions.explain: The Bible is seen as authoritative because it is believed to reveal God and to guide Christian life.

questions.q: A short, formal statement summarising Christian beliefs is called a...
questions.explain: A creed is a formal summary statement of Christian belief.

questions.q: The Nicene Creed is named after a Church council held in Nicaea in...
questions.explain: The Council of Nicaea met in 325 AD and produced the Nicene Creed.

questions.q: One reason the early Church produced creeds was to...
options: summarise and protect the core beliefs of Christianity
questions.explain: Creeds were written to state clearly and safeguard the essential beliefs of the faith.

questions.q: Emma believes she experiences God directly whenever she prays. This is best described as an example of...
questions.explain: A direct personal experience of God through prayer is a form of special revelation.

questions.q: David studies the order and design of the natural world and concludes that God exists. This best illustrates...
questions.explain: Knowing God through observing the natural world and reason is general revelation.

questions.q: During Sunday worship a congregation stands together and recites the Apostles' Creed. This best shows the Church...
options: publicly declaring its shared beliefs about God
rejecting the authority of the Bible
questions.explain: Reciting a creed in worship is a way the Church publicly affirms its shared beliefs.
